about: Corrections to matn.diacritized, the reading text; matn.arabic is the source verbatim. Made by pipeline/diacritize/fix_reading_text.py.

radiya-allahu.description: «رَضِيَ اللَّهُ»: Allah is the subject, not «اللَّهِ»

salla-allahu.description: «صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ»: Allah is the subject, not «اللَّهِ»

ani-bni.description: «عَنِ ابْنِ»: genitive after the preposition, not «عَنْ ابْنُ»

allahu-subject.description: Allah as the subject of «قَالَ»، «يَقُولُ»، «رَحِمَهُ», not «اللَّهِ»

dotless-radiya.description: the source's «رضى الله» read as the noun «رِضًى اللَّهِ»; «رَضِيَ اللَّهُ»

dotless-kunya.description: the source's kunya «أبى» read as the verb «أَبَى»; «أَبِي» after «عَنْ»/«بْنُ», with the name after it in the genitive

repeated-honorific.description: the source repeats half the honorific: «وسلمى الله عليه وسلم» reads «وَسَلَّمَ»

source-typo.description: a misspelt word in the source: «حتي» → «حَتَّى», «إلىس» → «أَلَيْسَ», «امراتى» → «امْرَأَتِي»

garbled-alif-maqsura.description: «حَتَّى» and «عَلَى» given the marks of another word («حَتْىً»، «عِلَىْ»)

reviewed.description: a word reviewed in context: a ya-word the diacritizer gave a fatha (read «ā»), an active verb read as passive, or a wrong case beside it

dotless-ya.description: a final «ى» read as a ya, written «ي»: after a kasra («فِى» → «فِي») or with its own mark («رَضِىَ» → «رَضِيَ»), and the letter name «الزَّاي»

citation-stop.description: a full stop before the closing citation («رَوَاهُ …», «مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِ»), which is not part of the hadith
